quote: 国王はシヴァ神のために廟を立て、その形像を描き
finding: Nagasawa (長沢和俊, 東洋文庫 法顕伝・宋雲行紀) translates 濕婆仙 as the god Śiva: the king built a shrine for Śiva and painted his image. This is the page K. Harimoto cites.

topic: Songyun: 除灰 perhaps 塗灰
quote: 灰を除くは灰を塗るの誤りかも知れない
finding: Nagasawa's note: 'removing ash' may be an error for 'smearing ash', and he connects it with a Hindu sect of ash-smearers who worship Śiva. So the Śaiva and ash-smearer reading is already his.

quote: この山はジャータカに現われる葉波国の、湿波 (シヴァ Si
finding: Nagasawa notes that the mountain is where Sudāna, son of King 湿波 of 葉波国 in the jātaka, was exiled. Caveat: the 濕婆仙 protecting the stūpa could echo the jātaka's royal family rather than the god, although 仙 and the ash point to a Śaiva ascetic or deity.
Nagasawa: Faxian's 達嚫 = Dakṣiṇa, location unknown, 200 yojanas S of Kauśāmbī, so a country of the Deccan.

quote: 跋邏末羅耆釐山 (Bhrāmara-giri, 黒峰山)に至る
finding: Nagasawa compares Faxian's five-storeyed rock monastery with Xuanzang's Bhramaragiri, which he glosses 黒峰山/黒峯 ('black peak'); Taishō and CBETA read 黑蜂 ('black bee'). K. Harimoto's 黒峰 probably comes from Nagasawa's rendering, not from a variant reading. Nagasawa also cites Huichao's three-storeyed rock monastery built for Nāgārjuna in South India.

quote: パーラーヴァタはサンスクリットで「鳩」の意
finding: Nagasawa: 波羅越 = Pārāvata, 'pigeon' in Sanskrit.

quote: O Maheśvara, you will be [active] when the Kaliyuga arrives
finding: Bakker (Monuments of Hope, Gloom, and Glory in the Age of the Hunnic Wars, Gonda Lecture 2016, publ. 2017, p. 15), quoting Eltschinger 2014: in the Kāraṇḍavyūha, Avalokiteśvara prophesies that Maheśvara will be the creator in the Kali age. This is the background to Potalaka's Avalokiteśvara appearing as 自在天 or as an ash-smearer ("Hans' article" in K. Harimoto's note).
